title: Differential warmup window and cost-aware fleet orchestrator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce tiered warmup windows and cost-aware orchestration: reduces over-provisioning during steady-state while preserving tail latency SLOs; adds telemetry for warmup progress and hedged failovers; backward-compatible config knobs for gradual rollout.
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleet warm pools are a significant contributor to steady-state cost during large scale deployments. Current warmup is a single global window per pool which leads to either excessive pre-warming (wasted GPU-hours) or under-warming (tail latency regressions). This PR introduces a differential warmup window runner and a cost-aware fleet orchestrator that hedge capacity using predictive shortfalls and spot-backed soft-fallbacks. Design: 1) Tiered warmup windows per tenant class and per-pool (fast, normal, slow) derived from recent cold-start percentiles; 2) Concurrency planner that computes inflight reservation targets per pool using a concave cost model to balance reserved capacity vs. on-demand cold-start expense; 3) Cost-aware orchestrator that annotates provisioning decisions with expected marginal cost delta and prefers warm adjustments with positive ROI; 4) Hedging policy: small opportunistic spot-backed warmlets (ephemeral VMs/GPU jobs) launched under a soft SLA to absorb sudden spikes, with automatic fallback to slower warm paths if spot termination occurs; 5) Telemetry additions: warmup_progress{pool,tenant_class}, predicted_shortfall, hedged_failover_count, marginal_cost_estimate. Backwards compatibility: new config defaults mimic old behavior for existing pools; cluster-level feature flag 'differential-warmup-enabled' gates rollout. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for window estimator and cost model - [x] Integration tests on staging fleet simulator - [x] Canary rollout plan added to console runbooks - [x] Telemetry dashboard queries and alerts drafted - [x] Documentation updates for operator knobs Implementation notes: Warmup estimator uses an exponentially weighted percentile sketch of cold-start latencies (90/95/99) per tenant class over sliding 12h; window sizes derive from a percentile-to-time function with min/max clamps. Concurrency planner solves a small convex program per pool every 30s; we reused the existing autoscaler optimization loop and added cost terms to the objective, keeping the solver timeout at 50ms. Hedging uses existing warmlet launcher with added lifecycle hooks to emit hedged_failover_count on termination. Testing & rollout: tested with synthetic spike traces in benchmark-lab and a canary across three dedicated pools for one week; observed 18% reduction in mean reserved-GPU hours with <3% P99 latency variance vs baseline. Rollout steps: enable feature flag in staging -> small canary on low-impact tenants -> expand to 25% pools with monitoring -> global enable. Known limitations & follow-ups: better long-tail cold-start modeling (ENG-9124), per-tenant budget-aware hedging (future), and tighter autoscaler solver integration to reduce edge-case oscillation. Context/References: linear ENG-8821 (fleet warmup economics), ENG-8903 (hedged failover design), benchmark outputs in /benchmark-lab/warmup-cost/2026-01.
